Melee vs. Ranged Lanes

Laning as a melee champion against a ranged one feels unfair, but it's very playable. Learn how to survive and win as the melee side, and how to punish melee champions when you're the ranged one.

Why this matchup feels unfair

A ranged champion can hit you from outside your reach. Every time you walk up to last-hit, they get a free basic attack on you. Over a few waves, that adds up to a lot of lost health. This is called poke.

But melee champions have their own advantages. Most are tankier, many have dashes or crowd control to close the gap, and once they reach you, they usually win the fight up close. So the matchup becomes a simple question: can the ranged champion keep you away long enough, or can you survive until you're strong enough to get in?

You'll see this most in top lane, where champions like Garen or Darius face Teemo, Quinn or Vayne, and in mid lane, where melee assassins like Yasuo or Talon face long-range mages like Xerath.

As melee: survive the early levels

Your first goal isn't to win the lane. It's to reach your strong points without falling far behind.

  • Give up some CS. You don't need every minion. Prioritize cannon and melee minions, which are worth more. If a caster minion means taking a free attack and a spell, skip it. Stay close enough to get the experience, though: you get XP from minions dying nearby even if you don't last-hit them.
  • Start with sustain. Doran's Shield and a Health Potion is the classic melee start in a hard matchup. It restores some health after you take damage from an enemy champion, which is exactly what poke does. The rune Second Wind does a similar job.
  • Use the brush. Standing in a lane bush hides you. The ranged champion can't see you to attack you, can't aim their spells well, and has to guess when you'll walk out. Just remember they may ward it.
  • Let the wave come to you. Melee champions usually want the wave near their own tower. Then the ranged champion has to walk far forward to farm, which makes them easier to reach and easier for your jungler to gank.
Common mistakeWalking up to every last hit at full speed and taking a free attack each time. By level 3 you're at half health without having hit your opponent once. Time your steps forward so you arrive just as the minion is ready to die, then step back.

As melee: when and how to trade

You can't trade at range, so you have to pick your moments.

  • Trade when they last-hit. When the ranged champion attacks a minion, they can't attack you for a moment. Walk in, hit them, and walk out. Short trades are your friend; long fights near their wave aren't.
  • Trade when their key spell is down. Once Teemo has used his blind and it has worn off, your basic attacks work again until it comes back. If Vayne uses her knockback, she can't push you away again for some time.
  • Use your tools to block or dodge. Yasuo's wind wall stops most projectiles, so a mage like Xerath has a much harder time hitting him while it's up.
  • Wait for your spikes. Many melee champions get much stronger at level 2 or 3 when their combo is complete, at level 6 with their ultimate, and again with their first completed item. Until then, farm and stay healthy.
Pro tipSome melee champions, like Nasus, barely need to trade at all early. Against a ranged opponent, they farm safely under their tower, stay even on experience and win the game later. Losing the lane a little is fine if you still get your scaling.

As melee: buy the right defenses and ask for help

Items can turn a bad lane around. If the ranged champion deals most of their damage with basic attacks, like Vayne, Quinn or Caitlyn, Plated Steelcaps cut the damage from every attack. If they deal magic damage, like Teemo or Kennen, Mercury's Treads help a lot.

Ranged champions in these matchups often have weak escapes and push up the lane to poke. That makes them great gank targets. Let your jungler know:

  • Ping your lane when the enemy is pushed forward with no vision.
  • Keep the wave near your tower so the gank doesn't need to go deep.
  • Have your crowd control ready when your jungler arrives.

One successful gank can flip the whole lane, because the ranged champion now has to respect you too.

As ranged: punish the melee champion

If you're the ranged side, your job is to make every minion expensive for your opponent.

  • Auto them when they walk up for CS. Each time a melee champion steps forward to last-hit, they're in your range and you're not in theirs. Hit them, then go back to farming. Do this every wave and they'll either lose a lot of farm or have to recall early.
  • Watch minion aggro. Hitting a champion near their minions makes those minions attack you. Step back after each attack so you don't take free minion damage.
  • Keep the wave on your side. When the wave sits near your tower, the melee champion has to walk a long way to reach you, taking attacks the whole time, and they're far from their own safety. You can push into their tower when you want to recall or take plates, but that leaves you further from home, so do it when you know where their jungler is.
  • Spend your mana on poke, not on pushing. Clearing the wave with spells pushes it toward them, which is often exactly what the melee champion wants.

As ranged: respect the all-in

Poking a melee champion down is only half the job. If they get on top of you at the wrong time, they can still win.

  • Know their all-in level. If their combo comes online at level 3 or their ultimate at level 6, play further back when they reach it, especially if they hit it first.
  • Track their gap-closer. Most melee champions have one dash, jump or speed boost to reach you. When it's on cooldown, you can play forward. When it's up, keep a safe distance.
  • Don't let them stack items for free. If they buy armor or magic resist, your poke does less. Use your item lead to take plates or help your jungler instead of trading forever.
  • Remember summoner spells. A melee champion with Flash or Ghost up can close more distance than you expect. If you've seen them use Flash, you have about five minutes of extra safety.
Common mistakePoking a melee champion to half health, then walking forward to finish them off. That's often exactly the fight they wanted. Keep poking from range or back off, and let them come to you.

Key takeaways

  • As melee, give up some CS, prioritize cannons and melee minions, and stay in XP range.
  • Start with Doran's Shield and potions, use the brush, and let the wave come to your side.
  • Trade when the ranged champion last-hits or uses a key spell, and wait for your level and item spikes.
  • Ask your jungler for help: ranged laners who push forward are easy gank targets.
  • As ranged, hit them every time they walk up for CS, keep the wave on your side, and respect their all-in level.
